title: Where does the lift end after a wrong press?
description: A child in the Toy Store presses the plus button twice by mistake and then the minus button three times. The two sets of presses are written as plus two and minus three and added to find the total movement. Keeko thinks the lift ends one floor up because the first press was plus, and the longer movement breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: presses made one after another combine by adding their signed numbers. Watch for students who keep the sign of the first press.

source: Gurmit was in the Toy Store and wanted to go down two floors
video_script.why: A child learns that combining button presses is adding signed numbers, because every later sum of integers is a combined movement.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lift, with two plus presses followed by three minus presses from the Toy Store
video_script.anchor: Ziva in the lift of Ruhee, starting at the Toy Store, floor −1
video_script.wrong_answer: the lift ends one floor up
video_script.wrong_move: keeps the sign of the first press instead of comparing the two movements
video_script.payoff_line: The longer movement decides whether the lift ends higher or lower.

final_answer.value: One floor below the Toy Store (one floor down). (+2) + (−3) = −1.
final_answer.spoken: one floor below the Toy Store

names.Ziva: pressed plus twice then minus three times from the Toy Store and ended one floor below it
names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: one floor below the Toy Store; (+2) + (−3) = −1
never_show: the total movement before the answer
maths_rules: Two plus presses are +2; three minus presses are −3.
(+2) + (−3) = −1: two floors up and three floors down leave one floor down.
Check: from the Toy Store (−1), two floors up is the Food Court (+1), and three floors down is the Video Games shop (−2), one floor below the Toy Store.
video_script.design: One idea: presses made one after another add up to one movement. One lift picture throughout; the two movements are drawn as bars up and down. Keeko's doubt is broken by comparing the two bars.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the lift ends one floor up, because the first press was plus.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>But compare the two movements. Three floors down is more than two floors up.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The longer movement wins, so the lift ends lower than it began.
